notes.title: Public Demo Hot Fix #2
notes.content:
[h3]Major Performance Improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Blobs now take up less memory and no longer tank framerate when spawning (can still happen occasionally).
[*] Some feature checks that were done per frame are now done via events such as if each element in a cluster was painted yet or not.
[*] Realistic physics drag is now done over multiple frames, are time sliced (no longer all happen on the same frames), and is no longer always active.
[*] Made several non-static environmental elements static to help with performance.
[*] Rebaked occlusion culling to have an updated rendering culling throughout the map.
[/list]

[h3]Minor Fix:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The input icon for abilities was also showing as Left Mouse Button rather than Right Mouse Button.
[*] Added captions to the intro video, this is primarily in preparation for localization, but also just for convenience!
[*] Removed several falling physics objects that clipped through the world.
[*] Removed several small physics objects that didn't meaningfully contribute to gameplay (besides hurting frame rates).
[/list]

[*] Stepping on multiple different surfaces can cause audio popping

[/list]

[h3]One major known issue I'm still investigating:[/h3]

[list]
[*] Added story teaser as a skippable intro to the game

Okay... maybe this was a lot. But that's probably a good thing!

notes.title: Pre-Release Demo
notes.content:
Honestly too many changes to count but basically the biggest ones are:
[list]
[*]Characters added that you can have conversations with
[*]Areas now spawn keys and those key are use to unblock specific progress points
[*]Added a tutorial level to showcase the basics in a less cluttered way
[*]Removed a lot of enemies so only specific areas have those kinds of dangers
[*]Abilities now must be discovered in the map rather than unlocked
[*]Added some micro quests that you can get from characters
[*]Rebalanced paint use, ink flask charges, blobs, and the fill rate of many objects to feel better
[*]Tons and tons of bug fixes
[/list]

This is just what I could squeeze in the scope up to the 14th since that's when journalist access to the event begins. I will keep refining and fixing bugs up to the 24th when the event begins!

notes.title: Internal Testing for Public Demo
notes.content:
This is just the most necessary changes needed to make this testable in full, here are some key changes:

[list]
[*] Areas now have a tracker for how many objects are painted and filled
[*] When an area is filled in sufficiently then a yellow "Key" object is spawned
[*] There are new gating that requires these yellow "Key" objects to open paths
[*] Added the Sword Relic and Bow Relic to the map to be discovered and used to traverse the layers of the map
[*] Enemies are now stunned when painted red temporarily, but can still be permanently defeated with the Sword Relic
[*] Changed the model on the boat that ends the demo to something more eye catching
[*] When rewards are spawned from filling the environment there are trails that draw attention to them
[/list]

Additional changes are primarily bug fixes, flow changes, replacing some old models with new ones, and adding a fish man to meet in the gazebo. Normal stuff.

notes.title: A Series of Polish Changes
notes.content:
This demo is not meaningfully different content wise than the previous, but a lot has been reworked.

The last demo added several new mechanics like the sword and the bow abilities, that are removed for now and should be available from additional content being added.

Key Changes:
[list]
[*] More auto-filling objects around
[*] More sources of paint refill
[*] Running out of paint doesn't kill you
[*] When low on paint your first health bar will regenerate when not painting
[*] Added relaxing soundtrack
[*] New upgrade system paid for with the crystals you find in the map
[*] Streamlined level - Removed a lot of ancillary areas and kept it to one key loop
[*] Rebalanced how quickly things fill with paint and made paint drain much more slowly
[*] Make the player faster
[*] Completely reworked the character controller
[*] Added more feedback when rewards are given or when things are filled
[*] Added a state for filled in objects to show when they are "Complete" (they fill white)
[*] Added stationary enemies to add some tension and threat of death in distinct areas
[/list]

One thing I had hoped to have completed by now was dialogue with characters. I went down a route with trying to add too many new things rather than focusing on getting that up and running. I have since re-prioritized.

The next build will be a true vertical slice in this first area, even adding things that are meant to be added in later levels, with the hopes of that being the Next Fest demo (in February).

Thanks so much for playing and don't forget to "Press F6 to submit feedback"!

notes.title: Major Gameplay Shifts!
notes.content:
[h3]Each color now has a unique ability[/h3]
[list]
[*] Green - Paint the environment, grow natural elements
[*] Red - Sword Swipe that can break elements that block progress
[*] Blue - A big paint explosion that can quickly activate elements through time
[/list]
This is to make each color have more of a unique identity and something new to build puzzles off of as well as future upgrades.

Each color still maintains their themes: red is violence and action, green is nature and growth, blue is time and gravity. These abilities should make it easier to reinforce these themes and add new unique elements in the future.

[h3]Additional Gameplay Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Multiple breakable elements in the game now give you blobs of paint that can refill your paint on your journey.
[*] The starting area is gated until you unlock the red ability.
[*] There are now more generous ability upgrades.
[*] The former shrines that refilled paint on your journey are now respawn points. You must now find real trees that will refill your paint.
[*] The flow of the early resource management is more forgiving at the start
[*] Fall damage is now non-lethal, but still drains paint
[*] Several level design elements have been changed to make the level flow more clear
[*] Groundwork is laid to swap the current simplistic paint amount upgrades into resources that let you unlock different upgrades to match your playstyle/strategy for exploration
[/list]

[*] As stated above you can lock the brush to center screen if this default mode still causes any motion sickness
[/list]
